6.  
At about 1529 hours, I arrived at Tai Po Baptist Public School inside Wang Fuk Court and took on the role of Incident Commander of the No.3 Alarm Fire as per the established principle stipulated in General Orders 41. At the material time, I noted that fire had scattered on the middle and upper portions of the scaffoldings installed along the external walls of the east façade of Wang Sun House and southeast façades of Wang Kin House and Wang Shing House; whilst fire had spread along the scaffoldings on the southwest façade of Wang Cheong House and east façade of Wang Tai House. Burning bamboo sticks and debris continuously fell from height, piling up on the open ground.  

[FS D/G(I)/3]  
pp. 22-26  
(A.S. No.211, 22-26)  

[Question 7(b)]  
7.  
At about 1532 hours, I met Assistant Divisional Officer CHEUNG Lok-hang (“ADO CHEUNG”) at the roundabout inside Wang Fuk Court and he reported that a Mayday message was received by Senior Station Officer HUI Kin-on (“SStnO HUI”) at about 1522 hours via radiotelephone (“R/T”). Nevertheless, the Mayday caller’s identity and location could not be recognised in the message. In order to clarify the Mayday caller’s identity and location, SStnO HUI promptly responded via R/T but with no response from the caller. SStnO HUI formed 5 Emergency Response Teams (“ERTs”) in attempt to conduct Mayday rescue operations on 30/F of Wang Cheong House, but the ERTs could not enter Wang Cheong House as its front entrance and rear exit were blocked by burning bamboo sticks and debris. As such, crew members were tackling the fire in order to establish a clear access.
